topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the significance and conceptual complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overarching organization, nomenclature conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct biochemical pathways that initiate complement activation and converge at the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector functions of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the protective regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the clinical phenotypes and disease pathologies associated with deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms pathogens deploy to resist complement-mediated clearance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
